mainTopic: The משנה on whether a replaced חטאת is left to die for a יחיד and for the ציבור, and what happens to the leftover animal when someone has two valid חטאות
overview: The amud opens by finishing a count of years from the previous page. שמואל, שאול and דוד together reach forty years. Then a new משנה rules that a private (יחיד) חטאת whose owner already got כפרה with a replacement animal is left to die, but a communal (ציבור) one is not. רבי יהודה says even the communal one dies. רבי שמעון compares this case to the other 'dying חטאות', which apply only to a יחיד. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק: when there are two valid חטאות, the owner may bring either one, but only one. It then asks what happens to the leftover animal. רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says it grazes and רבי שמעון says it dies. Since רבי יהודה says 'die' in the משנה, the גמרא tries switching the names, but that clashes with רבי שמעון's rule of five dying חטאות. It then gives two answers: either the two rulings deal with different cases, or רבי יהודה is explaining the views of רבי and of the רבנן. Finally, the גמרא asks in surprise whether anyone really holds that a communal חטאת is left to die. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Adding up the forty years of kings
steps.stepSummary: The count from the previous page ends: ten years of שמואל alone, one year of שאול with שמואל, two years of שאול alone, and thirty-seven years of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ten years שמואל ruled alone, one year שאול ruled while שמואל was alive, two years שאול ruled alone, and thirty-seven years דוד ruled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a calculation it started on the previous page by adding up the years of leadership. This closes that discussion before a new משנה begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four numbers add up to forty: 10 + 1 + 2 + 37. This explains which forty years the earlier discussion meant, counting from when the people first asked for a king.

keyTerms.meaning: ruled / reigned
by himself, alone

phrases.english: Ten years Samuel reigned by himself,
phrases.notes: This finishes a count from the previous page: how we get to forty years since the people asked for a king.

phrases.english: one year that Saul and Samuel reigned,
and two that Saul reigned by himself,
and thirty-seven that David reigned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the calculation begun on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The forty years are made up of 10 + 1 + 2 + 37 years of leadership.

steps.title: A private sin offering dies, a communal one does not
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a יחיד's חטאת whose owner already got כפרה with another animal is left to die, but a ציבור's is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A private חטאת whose owners already got atonement is left to die. But a communal one is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts with the first opinion (the תנא קמא). It gives one rule for a private חטאת and a different rule for a communal one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that certain חטאות can never be offered and are left to die. One of them is a חטאת that was lost and replaced, so the owner already got כפרה with the replacement. The משנה says this rule applies to a private person's חטאת, not to the community's.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
a sin offering brought by a private individual
whose owners already got atonement (with a different animal)
is left to die (it cannot be offered or used)
the community

steps.confusionAlert: 'Left to die' does not mean someone kills it. The animal is locked away until it dies by itself, because it can never be offered or used.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An individual's sin offering whose owners achieved atonement is left to die,
phrases.notes: He means the owner lost this animal, brought a replacement, and was already forgiven through the replacement.

phrases.english: but one of the community is not left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the year count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A replaced private חטאת is left to die; a replaced communal חטאת is not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even the communal one dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and says a communal חטאת in this case is also left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It shall die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the תנא קמא. He holds that a communal חטאת whose owners already got כפרה is also left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is only about the community's animal. For רבי יהודה, the rule about a replaced חטאת applies to the community too, so there is no difference between יחיד and ציבור here.

keyTerms.meaning: it shall die (be left to die)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It shall die.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the communal חטאת from the line before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's rule for the community.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a communal חטאת whose owners already got כפרה is left to die.

steps.title: רבי שמעון compares to the other dying sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון supports the first opinion. The other dying חטאות apply only to a יחיד, so this one and the one whose year passed are also only for a יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: We find that the offspring of a חטאת, the substitute of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owners died are rules said about a private person, not the community. So too, a חטאת whose owners got atonement and one whose year passed are rules said about a private person, not the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון brings a comparison ('מה מצינו') to back up the first opinion. He also adds a second case: a חטאת that is past its first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three of the five dying חטאות clearly apply only to a private person. רבי שמעון reasons that the other two (owner got כפרה, year passed) should work the same way. So none of the five apply to the community.

keyTerms.meaning: 'just as we find' — learning one case from similar cases
the offspring born to a חטאת animal
an animal someone tried to swap for a חטאת
whose owners died
its (first) year has passed, so it is too old to be offered

steps.whatToRemember: All five dying חטאות: the offspring, the substitute, owner died, owner already got כפרה, year passed. רבי שמעון holds that all five apply only to a יחיד, never to the ציבור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Just as we found with the offspring of a sin offering,
and with the substitute for a sin offering,
and with a sin offering whose owners died —
the matters are stated about an individual and not about the community,
so too, one whose owners achieved atonement and one whose year has passed —
the matters are stated about an individual and not about the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה by supporting the first opinion and widening it.
steps.raayaObject: That a replaced חטאת (and one whose year passed) is left to die only for a יחיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The other dying חטאות (offspring, substitute, owner died), which apply only to a יחיד.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks about two valid sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It asks what the פסוק 'יביא... לחטאת' teaches: if a lost חטאת is found after a replacement was set aside, where do we learn that he may bring whichever one he wants?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: What does the פסוק mean when it says 'חטאת... יביא'? If someone set aside his חטאת, it got lost, he set aside another in its place, and then the first one was found, so both are standing there, where do we learn that he may bring whichever one he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that sets up a case: two valid חטאות for one sin. It asks for the source that he may choose either one. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the background case for the משנה's 'owner already got כפרה' rule. Before we know what happens to the leftover animal, we must know that he may pick either one to offer.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
from where (do we learn this)?
it was lost
he set aside (an animal as an offering)

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
What does it mean when it says 'sin offering... he shall bring'?
From where is it derived for one who consecrated his sin offering and it was lost,
and he separated another in its place,
and the first one was found alive,
and both of them are standing —
from where is it derived that he may bring whichever of them he wishes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the case behind the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that either of two valid חטאות may be brought.

steps.title: The word חטאת: either one may be brought
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word 'חטאת' in the פסוק teaches he may bring whichever one he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with the word 'חטאת' from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חטאת' is general. It does not point to one specific animal, so whichever of the two he picks counts as his חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches (by saying)

phrases.english: The verse states: 'A sin offering.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'חטאת' allows him to bring either animal.

steps.title: Maybe he must bring both?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a possible mistake: maybe he has to bring both animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he should bring both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wrong idea, that both animals must be brought. This sets up the next part of the פסוק to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals are holy and both are fit to be offered. So one could think both must go on the מזבח. The ברייתא raises this only so it can show from the פסוק why it is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'one might think' — a wrong idea the ברייתא is about to reject

phrases.english: One might think he should bring both of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible wrong idea after step 6's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether both animals must be offered.

steps.title: 'יביאנה' — only one, not two
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יביאנה' (he shall bring it) teaches that he brings only one animal, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He shall bring it' — one, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea of bringing both, using the word 'יביאנה' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'It' is singular, so only one animal is offered. That leaves a second, extra animal behind. Its status is the next question the גמרא takes up.

keyTerms.meaning: he shall bring it (singular)
one and not two

steps.whatToRemember: With two valid חטאות: the word 'חטאת' teaches he may choose either one, and 'יביאנה' teaches he brings only one. The גמרא next asks what happens to the leftover animal.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'He shall bring it' —
one and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wrong idea raised in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only one of the two animals is brought, learned from the singular word 'יביאנה'.

steps.title: What happens to the second animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what we do with the animal that was not brought as the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that second animal, what happens to it?
steps.whatsHappening: We just learned that he brings only one animal. Now the גמרא asks what we do with the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two animals: the lost one that was found, and the replacement. Only one is brought. The leftover one cannot just be ignored, because it was set aside as a קרבן. So the גמרא needs a ruling on what to do with it.

keyTerms.meaning: the second one, here meaning the leftover animal that was not brought
what will be with it? A standard way of asking what its status is

phrases.english: And that second animal
what will be with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 8. Since only one animal is brought, the status of the other is now unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal fate of the animal that was set aside but not brought.

steps.title: A ברייתא with two opinions: graze or die
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says the animal grazes, and רבי שמעון says it is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said that a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says it is left to graze, and רבי שמעון says it is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא that brings two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Graze' means the animal is kept until it gets a blemish. Then it is redeemed, and the money is used for a voluntary קרבן. 'Die' means it is locked away until it dies. רבי שמעון fits his view from step 4, that a יחיד's חטאת whose owner already got כפרה with another animal is left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: it shall graze, meaning it is kept until it gets a blemish and is then redeemed
a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is left to graze,
Rabbi Shimon says: it is left to die.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מחלוקת: רבי יהודה says it grazes, and רבי שמעון says it dies.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה elsewhere says it dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can say 'graze' here, when elsewhere we heard him say 'it dies.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יהודה really say it grazes? But we heard רבי יהודה say 'it dies'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא, because it seems to contradict what רבי יהודה says in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה rules that this kind of חטאת is left to die. The ברייתא has him saying the opposite. One חכם cannot hold both views in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: but did he really say? An opening that signals a contradiction
we heard him say, meaning we know his view from another source

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yehuda say it is left to graze?
But we heard Rabbi Yehuda say 'it shall die'!
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in the ברייתא of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view of 'graze' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts his ruling of 'die' in the משנה.

steps.title: Switch the names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reversing the names: רבי יהודה says 'die' and רבי שמעון says 'graze.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי יהודה says it dies, and רבי שמעון says it grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: To fix the contradiction, the גמרא swaps the two names in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the names are reversed, רבי יהודה now says 'die' in both places, so his problem is solved. But this moves the 'graze' view onto רבי שמעון, and that sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: reverse, meaning swap the names of who said what

phrases.english: Reverse it:
Rabbi Yehuda says: it is left to die,
Rabbi Shimon says: it is left to graze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by changing the names in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's names are set as written.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swap the names so that רבי יהודה consistently says 'die.'

steps.title: But רבי שמעון says five חטאות die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי שמעון cannot say 'graze,' since he listed five חטאות that are left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי שמעון really say it grazes? But רבי שמעון said: five חטאות are left to die!
steps.whatsHappening: The swap creates a new problem. Now רבי שמעון contradicts his own famous rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's list of five dying חטאות includes a חטאת whose owner already got כפרה with another animal. That is exactly our case. So he cannot hold 'graze,' and the swap fails.

keyTerms.meaning: the five kinds of חטאת that are left to die

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Shimon say it is left to graze?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon said: five sin offerings are left to die!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reversal proposed in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reversed version, in which רבי שמעון says 'graze.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's rule of five dying חטאות covers this case, so he must say 'die.'

steps.title: Keep the names: two different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the ברייתא as written. רבי יהודה's two rulings deal with different cases: when the animal was lost only when the replacement was set aside, or when it was still lost at the time of כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really do not reverse it, and there is no difficulty. Here, it was lost at the time the replacement was set aside. There, it was lost at the time of כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the swap. It explains that רבי יהודה's two rulings are not a contradiction, because they deal with two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא ('graze'), the animal was lost when the replacement was set aside but was found before the replacement was brought. In the משנה ('die'), the animal was still lost when the replacement was brought for כפרה. Because it was found earlier, the first case is gentler.

keyTerms.meaning: really, meaning we go back to the original version
it is not difficult, meaning the contradiction falls away
setting aside an animal as a קרבן
atonement, here the time the replacement is actually brought
lost

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve the same lost animal. The only difference is when it was found: before the replacement was brought (graze), or only after it was brought (die).

phrases.english: Rather, really do not reverse it,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
here, it was lost at the time of setting aside,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא, which says the animal grazes. It turned up before the replacement was brought.

phrases.english: there, it was lost at the time of atonement.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה, which says it's left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the reversal of step 12 and answers the original challenge of step 11 another way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's 'graze' and 'die' refer to the same case and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Graze' applies when the animal was found before כפרה, and 'die' applies when it was still lost at כפרה.

steps.title: Another answer: רבי יהודה following רבי or the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Both sources deal with an animal lost only when the replacement was set aside. רבי יהודה says 'die' according to רבי, and 'graze' according to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: both deal with the time of setting aside, and there is no difficulty. This is רבי יהודה following רבי, and that is רבי יהודה following the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to solve רבי יהודה's contradiction. It does not split the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the case is the same in both sources. The difference is whose view רבי יהודה is explaining. רבי holds that even an animal lost only when the replacement was set aside is left to die, so the משנה follows him. The רבנן hold it is left to die only if it was still lost at כפרה, so the ברייתא's 'graze' follows them.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say, an opening for an alternative answer
this one and that one, meaning both sources
according to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's 'graze' and 'die' do not contradict each other. Either they deal with different cases (found before or after כפרה), or he is explaining two different views (the רבנן or רבי).

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
both this and that are about the time of setting aside,
and it is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Yehuda according to Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who argues with the רבנן in a משנה later in this מסכת. This side matches our משנה, where it's left to die.

phrases.english: that is Rabbi Yehuda according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 11, in place of step 14's split between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ruling to a different underlying opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the case is the same, the two rulings must contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה rules 'die' following רבי and 'graze' following the רבנן.

steps.title: Does anyone really say a communal sin offering is left to die?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view quoted in the משנה. It asks whether anyone truly holds that a חטאת צבור whose owners already got atonement is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there really anyone who says that a communal sin offering, whose owners already got atonement, is left to die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה and questions it. It asks, in surprise, whether anyone really holds that a communal חטאת is left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a חטאת צבור that was lost. The community brought another animal and got atonement with it, and then the first one turned up. The question 'is there anyone who says' signals that the ruling 'it dies' sounds strange for a communal offering, so the גמרא wants to know who could hold this.

keyTerms.meaning: "But is there anyone who says...?" A surprised challenge asking whether any sage really holds this view
A communal sin offering, brought for the whole community and not for one person
"The owners got atonement." Atonement was already done with a different animal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a simple request for information. The words 'is there anyone who says' are a challenge. The גמרא doubts that anyone holds this ruling.

phrases.english: But is there anyone who says
that a communal sin offering
whose owners achieved atonement is left to die?
phrases.notes: The 'owners' here are the community. They already got atonement with a different animal after this one was lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the earlier discussion of graze versus die for an individual's offering. It returns to the משנה's statement of רבי יהודה about a communal חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the משנה, given in the name of רבי יהודה, that even a חטאת צבור whose owners got atonement is left to die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea that a communal חטאת is left to die seems unheard of. The גמרא asks, in surprise, whether any sage actually holds it.
